episode_title: Apolo Ohno’s “Patient” Real Estate Investing Approach for Financial Freedom

real_qa.q: What caused Apollo Ono's major real estate investment loss in 2006-2008 and how did he recover?
real_qa.r: Apollo Ono invested in real estate through a fund between 2006 and 2008, writing promissory notes and loans, but the group committed mortgage fraud, including doctoring documents and falsifying information. He discovered this when a contact in Utah informed him that both principals had filed for personal bankruptcy without listing him as a creditor. He overcame this by radically owning the mistake rather than blaming the operators, then used that hard life lesson to compound his next generational move in real estate.

real_qa.r: Apollo Ono states that 80% of the Olympic athletes he knows from his cohort that have since retired and gone on to be successful are in real estate today, either in development, commercial real estate brokerage, residential real estate, or real estate development companies.

real_qa.q: What is the General Adaptation Syndrome principle Apollo Ono applies to entrepreneurship from athletic training?
real_qa.r: Apollo Ono describes the GAS principle—General Adaptation Syndrome—as alarm, resistance, then exhaustion. Growth happens when you recover a little bit before complete exhaustion. Unlike training 100% every day, athletes use periodization with large blocks of training volume followed by large blocks of recovery. Many entrepreneurs run never-ending block cycles until their decision-making quality falls apart, but this principle teaches that refreshed minds prevent burnout and sustain better performance.
real_qa.requete: General Adaptation Syndrome GAS principle entrepreneurship

real_qa.q: How long did Apollo Ono retire from speed skating before applying athletic lessons to real estate investing?
real_qa.r: Apollo Ono retired from speed skating 16 years ago and has since dedicated significant time to investing in real estate and building ventures at the intersection of high performance business and wellness. He applied the same rigor of hard work, discipline, and consistency that made him successful as an Olympic athlete to his business and investment endeavors.
real_qa.requete: Apollo Ono retired 16 years speed skating real estate

real_qa.q: What role does physiological optimization play in Apollo Ono's approach to entrepreneurial decision-making?
real_qa.r: Apollo Ono emphasizes that the fastest way to make a big life change is to change the body's feeling first, then behavior will follow through sleep, fueling, training, and breath—all controllable factors. When he was an Olympic athlete, his mental acuity and processing was extremely high because he lived a life attuned to physiological peak performance, which allowed his brain to make really good decisions. He still takes this seriously 16 years into retirement because optimal physiological state directly predicts quality of decision-making.

real_qa.q: Why does Apollo Ono advocate for patience as a key attribute in both short track speed skating and real estate?
real_qa.r: Apollo Ono states that patience is a key attribute toward a sport like short track speed skating and the same thing applies in real estate. Performance is cyclical, not linear—you move forward, fail, revert back, learn, and begin again in small circles building momentum. Understanding that performance cycles up and down helps entrepreneurs resist the urge to overtrade, exit positions prematurely, or make reactive decisions, instead allowing them to be patient and persist through cycles.
